observed_facts: DaVinci Resolve and Fusion

frameforge_implications: [INFERENCE] Attach evidence role and version to each extracted feature; a product page is not release-date evidence, and a current catalog is not a new publication.
limitations: [uncertain] Exact publication dates for undated product pages and exhaustive changes from 2025-10-24 through 2026-10-24 were not established. Search surfaced Resolve 20.3 named timeline snapshots and per-project Media Pool views, but the official forum release thread returned HTTP 403, so those claims are excluded from documented findings. A candidate announcement URL delivered only the site shell; search summaries were not promoted to verified release dates.
Only official public sources are cited. No community workaround or forum user statement is used as product documentation.

observed_facts: Inherited baseline (S3-S5): the Media Pool contains the project's clips. The Media page imports footage into that pool; the Edit page uses source clips in timelines. Bringing the current timeline shot to Fusion does not require exporting frames to another application.

Historical official baseline (S5, Lesson 1, printed pages 2-8): position the Edit playhead over the shot, click Fusion or press Shift-5. MediaIn represents the timeline source clip; MediaOut sends the composited image back to the Edit timeline. Disconnecting MediaOut makes the timeline clip blank because no image data reaches it.

Inherited baseline (S2): the Fusion clip timeline provides access to other clips in the Edit timeline without leaving Fusion. Additional media can be dragged from Media Pool bins into the graph (S2, S5). This is concrete shared media/timeline continuity, not an assertion that every page shares every selection.
Current Resolve 21 change (S1): Fusion-effect parameters can be adjusted directly in the Cut and Edit keyframe and curves editors; advanced VFX adjustments remain available on the Fusion page.

Inherited baseline (S4): ordinary bins organize project footage, Smart Bins remain current as matching media is added, and Power Bins make reusable graphics, logos, titles and clips available across projects on the system. These are different scopes, not equivalent production/channel identities.
frameforge_implications: [INFERENCE] Keep a production, timeline clip and asset identity stable when moving from editing into its graph. Preserve the selected clip, source range, playhead and output breadcrumb rather than creating an unrelated graph document.
[INFERENCE] Show whether an asset belongs to this production or a shared library. Keep channel identity and delivery credentials separate from reusable media bins.
limitations: [uncertain] Persistent selection, panel state, playhead and graph viewport behavior across every page switch and application restart were not established. No stable internal-ID schema, live-link model for all copies, or automatic rebinding after media replacement is claimed.
The Fusion MediaIn/MediaOut bridge does not establish that Color nodes use the same ports or graph objects.

observed_facts: Inherited baseline (S2, S5): Fusion nodes represent effects, generators, transforms, masks and image-processing operations. Connections determine compositing order and layering; moving a node visually without rewiring does not change the resulting image.

Historical official baseline (S5, Lesson 1, printed pages 9-12): a Merge node has a yellow background input, green foreground input, blue mask input, and square image output. Port positions can move around the node while their color/role stays meaningful. This describes those Fusion image/mask connectors, not a complete universal type system.

Historical official baseline (S5): the Inspector shows the selected tool's properties. A selected node has a red border; white dots indicate its assigned viewer. Loading an intermediate node into a viewer permits inspection independently of the final MediaOut result. A red selection border must not be misreported as an execution failure.

Historical official baseline (S5): the Fusion time ruler displays the source clip range and yellow render-range boundaries corresponding to the used timeline portion. A green line marks frames cached in RAM; RAM allocation limits cached playback duration. This is playback reuse, not durable task-execution evidence.

Inherited baseline (S2): Fusion has per-node versions selected using numbers at the top of the Inspector, allowing animation alternatives without duplicating a node. The graph can include expressions and modifiers linking parameters.

Scope boundary (S1, S7): Color's grading node editor, Resolve 21 layer-list view, MultiMaster trim operations and group pre-/post-clip grade versions are Color features. They are not documented as Fusion macro versions, compositing retry mechanisms or graph-layout features.
frameforge_implications: [INFERENCE] Make connector roles explicit with text/shape as well as color, and distinguish selected, previewed, cached, running and failed states.

[INFERENCE] Offer intermediate-output inspection and separate parameter variants from immutable execution runs. A run should capture graph revision, input artifact revisions, output evidence and errors; RAM cache alone is not that record.
limitations: [uncertain] A complete current typed-port catalog, durable per-node logs, cancellation propagation, partial retry semantics, cache invalidation guarantees and resumable execution evidence were not verified in the accessed official sections. Do not present Fusion as a general-purpose production DAG scheduler.

The integrated Fusion page and standalone Fusion Studio/render-node infrastructure are not conflated. No distributed rendering or cache-to-disk command is asserted for integrated Fusion on the strength of standalone documentation.

observed_facts: Inherited baseline (S3-S4): import local footage by dragging files or folders from storage into the project's Media Pool; folder structure can be retained. The Media page has a pre-import preview viewer and metadata inspector. No stock-footage discovery or licensed download marketplace is established by this import path.

Inherited baseline (S4): file- and frame-level metadata can be imported, viewed and edited; custom keywords, tags and metadata views support organization. Media display names can use scene/shot/take metadata without renaming source files.

Inherited baseline (S4): the clone tool makes bit-for-bit camera-media copies with checksum verification, including XXHash64, and can create multiple destination copies. This verifies copied bytes, not source authenticity or permission to reuse.

Current Resolve 21 change (S1): AI IntelliSearch analyzes media to find people, objects and dialogue keywords, presenting whole-clip results in the Media Pool. This searches existing media rather than granting rights or proving its origin.

Historical baseline (S5-S6): the official training guide is copyright 2025 and states all rights reserved for the book. Public access to training resources is not evidence of a blanket commercial redistribution license for accompanying footage. No lesson footage was downloaded.
frameforge_implications: [INFERENCE] Preserve source URL/provider ID, retrieval timestamp, content hash, original filename and media revision alongside editable production metadata.

[INFERENCE] Model source authenticity, byte-integrity verification, attribution obligations and commercial/derivative/redistribution permission as separate checks. Carry rights evidence through each derived clip and output.
limitations: [uncertain] The accessed official sources do not establish a machine-readable rights ledger, source-URL capture requirement, license verification, attribution enforcement or derivative/redistribution clearance in Resolve. General metadata support is not proof of those capabilities.
Actual footage licenses and retrieval receipts are not applicable to this documentation-only comparison: no footage was acquired.

observed_facts: Inherited baseline (S3): the Edit page combines a top-left Media Pool, left source viewer, right timeline viewer, timeline tracks, effects library and top-right Inspector. I/O mark source ranges; clips can be inserted, overwritten, replaced or layered in the timeline. Selecting a clip exposes its editable properties.

Historical official baseline (S5): Fusion has two viewers, a timebar and common-tool toolbar, a lower Node Editor and a right Inspector. The lower work area can show the Node Editor, Keyframes Editor or Spline Editor. Different nodes can be shown in the two viewers, enabling source/intermediate/final comparison.
Inherited baseline (S2): the Fusion clip strip navigates among Edit timeline shots without returning to Edit. Custom templates can be created in Fusion and used from Edit/Cut.
Current Resolve 21 change (S1): editing Fusion effects directly in Cut/Edit keyframe and curves editors reduces the need to enter Fusion for text, transitions and motion-graphics parameter changes.

Inherited baseline (S3): named/color-coded markers can include descriptions, keywords and durations; viewer annotations support drawing, highlights, text and shapes. These are review/context aids, not evidence of an immutable approval workflow.
frameforge_implications: [INFERENCE] A unified production workspace can combine asset bin, source/result preview, timeline, properties and graph as synchronized views of the same selected production object.

[INFERENCE] Expose safe routine controls in the editing Inspector; use a deliberate deeper graph view for structural changes. Keep the active clip name, time and result target visible during that switch.
limitations: [uncertain] Exact persistence of all selections, panel arrangements and scroll/zoom positions is not documented in the accessed sections. The sources do not show that all production data fits simultaneously in one screen.
This is documented layout and interaction, not an observation of usability, performance or runtime behavior on the current workstation.

observed_facts: Inherited baseline (S2): lower thirds, animated generators and transitions can be built as Fusion templates, added to the Edit effects library and reused in other projects. Create a macro from selected composition nodes, check parameters to expose, assign a custom name and save.

Inherited baseline (S2-S3): template authors decide which controls editors see on Edit. Editors can adjust title text, font, size and color through the Inspector; the stated purpose includes protecting design consistency while avoiding pre-rendered handoffs.

Current Resolve 21 change (S1): the Fusion macro editor adds an Inspector view for setting up, formatting and publishing macros. This is macro/tool publication for use in Resolve, not external channel publication.

Current Resolve 21 change (S1): Fusion effects are animatable from Cut/Edit keyframe and curves editors; the Fairlight Animator modifier can drive Fusion parameters using levels from timeline clips or Media Pool sources.
Inherited baseline (S4): Power Bins are cross-project reusable-asset collections; Smart Bins are metadata-driven views. Neither definition documents a video-channel account or credential boundary.

Scope boundary (S1): Color group-grade versions affect all clips in the grading group and have pre-/post-clip graph versions. They are not evidence that Fusion template instances remain live-linked to an updated macro definition.
frameforge_implications: [INFERENCE] Separate an immutable channel-template definition from production instances. Publish a constrained, labeled parameter schema for branding text, colors, logo and timing while keeping structural graph editing explicit.

[INFERENCE] Pin each production to a template revision by default, show available upgrades with a diff, and never silently update approved outputs. Keep destination/channel credentials outside reusable templates.
limitations: [uncertain] The accessed official sources establish reuse and exposed parameters but not package pinning, live propagation to existing instances, dependency migration, template-instance version compatibility or credential isolation. Do not assert copy-only or live-linked behavior without a specific contract.
YouTube/video-channel semantics are not applicable to Fusion macro authoring itself; broadcast branding reuse is documented, but a channel-owned template/credential model is not.

observed_facts: Inherited baseline (S2): Fusion node versions provide creative alternatives inside a composition. Inherited baseline (S4): the Deliver render queue supports multiple timelines/clips and multiple output versions; jobs may output audio/video, audio-only or video-only. These are different version/output layers.

Inherited baseline (S4): Quick Export can render and upload to configured YouTube, Vimeo or TikTok accounts after account information is entered in preferences. Custom export presets come from Deliver settings. Therefore local rendering and remote upload are distinct effects even when the UI combines them.

Current Resolve 21 Color-specific change (S1): MultiMaster trim management creates multiple HDR/SDR deliverables from one timeline. This must not be generalized into Fusion macro versioning or approval invalidation.

Current provider contract, not a Resolve implementation claim (S8): videos.insert requires an authorized scope such as https://www.googleapis.com/auth/youtube.upload; its response is a video resource. The retrieved page states a quota of 100 calls per day and 1 unit per call in the Video Uploads quota bucket. These are observed documentation values, not a measured account allowance or a claim about Resolve's client project.

Current provider contract (S8): status.privacyStatus is writable on upload. The retrieved insert documentation says omission defaults to public, with some uploads defaulting private based on creator account settings, and says unverified API projects are not restricted to private viewing mode. Accordingly a private upload default is not assumed for Resolve or FrameForge.

Current provider contract (S9-S10): a video has a unique id and snippet.channelId; publishedAt can differ from upload time. videos.list can retrieve specified IDs and requested status/snippet parts, enabling a separate read-back of destination identity and visibility. No such read-back was performed.
frameforge_implications: [INFERENCE] Separate creative node variants, timeline revision, rendered artifact revision, approval and provider publication. Approval should bind the exact artifact hash and production/template/input revisions, and become stale after relevant edits.

[INFERENCE] Make render-only, upload and publish separate explicit actions. Show destination channel, requested privacy, permission scope and exact artifact before the remote action; retain returned video ID and read back actual channel/visibility/status afterward.

[INFERENCE] Enforce an explicit safe visibility choice rather than trusting omission defaults. Refresh provider quota policy at implementation time; never derive remaining quota or granted scope from a product marketing page.
limitations: [uncertain] No immutable exact-artifact approval, edit-triggered approval invalidation, Resolve-specific OAuth scope list, destination permission check, default privacy setting, upload quota allocation or post-upload read-back guarantee was verified. Provider API documentation does not establish which calls Resolve makes.

Named timeline snapshots surfaced in search but are not included as verified because the official release thread could not be retrieved. Render queue versions must not be mislabeled as approved snapshots.
No account access, credential inspection, upload, publication or permission test occurred.

observed_facts: Historical official baseline (S5, Lesson 1): Shift-5 opens the Fusion page; 1 and 2 assign the selected node to left/right viewers. Ctrl-F on PC or Command-F on macOS frames the hovered viewer; + and - zoom viewers or Node Editor in steps. Ctrl-1/Ctrl-2 on PC or Command-1/Command-2 on macOS set viewer zoom to 100%/200%.

Historical official baseline (S5): Fusion keyboard and mouse commands are context-sensitive to pointer location. A red node outline indicates selection and white dots indicate viewer assignment. The Node Editor has an infinite work area and a Navigator pane for recentering off-screen nodes.
Inherited baseline (S2): Shift+Space opens Fusion tool search; 1/2 preview a selected node and tilde clears viewers. These Fusion shortcuts are not generalized to Color or every application page.

Inherited baseline (S3): keyboard customization lists available commands and assigned keys, offers other-application presets, and saves/exports custom presets. Historical baseline (S5) documents Workspace > Reset UI Layout.
Inherited baseline (S4): Media Pool bin views can be customized and multiple bin windows opened. This is desktop workspace adaptation, not evidence of responsive mobile layout.
frameforge_implications: [INFERENCE] Provide searchable/remappable commands, explicit keyboard focus and documented shortcuts for assets, timeline, graph, Inspector and preview; do not rely on invisible pointer location to determine destructive command scope.

[INFERENCE] Keep selection and preview assignment visually distinct and available through text/accessibility names, not color alone. Provide keyboard framing, zoom, minimap navigation and resettable layouts for dense graphs.
limitations: [uncertain] No WCAG conformance, screen-reader support, complete keyboard-only graph editing, focus order, contrast measurements, touch behavior or mobile responsiveness was verified. Color-coded selection/ports and mouse-oriented navigation are documented descriptions, not a compliance result.
Keyboard mappings may be changed by user presets; no shortcuts were exercised on a running application. Desktop pane customization does not prove small-screen reflow.
